root_cause.text: A logical negation error in the conditional check in `filesystems_freeze_callback()` within `fs/super.c` caused the function to freeze all filesystems when the intent was to freeze only those with the `FS_POWER_FREEZE` flag, by incorrectly writing `if (freeze_all_ptr && ...)` instead of `if (!freeze_all_ptr && ...)`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff changes `if (freeze_all_ptr && !(sb->s_type->fs_flags & FS_POWER_FREEZE))` to `if (!freeze_all_ptr && !(sb->s_type->fs_flags & FS_POWER_FREEZE))`. The commit message explains that the original check is reversed and causes all file systems to be frozen when `filesystem_freeze_enabled` is false.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:

Author: Christian Brauner <brauner@kernel.org>
Date:   Wed Nov 5 14:39:45 2025 +0100

    power: always freeze efivarfs
    
    The efivarfs filesystems must always be frozen and thawed to resync
    variable state. Make it so.
    
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251105-vorbild-zutreffen-fe00d1dd98db@brauner
    Signed-off-by: Christian Brauner <brauner@kernel.org>

diff --git a/fs/super.c b/fs/super.c
index 5bab94fb7e03..277b84e5c279 100644
bic_trace_step.reason: The added condition `if (freeze_all_ptr && !(sb->s_type->fs_flags & FS_POWER_FREEZE))` is the vulnerable construct: it returns early (skipping freeze) only when freeze_all_ptr is non-NULL and the filesystem lacks the FS_POWER_FREEZE flag. This is the inverse of the intended logic, which should return early only when not freezing all (`!freeze_all_ptr`) and the filesystem lacks the flag. As a result, when `freeze_all` is false, no filesystem is skipped, freezing everything; when `freeze_all` is true, only FS_POWER_FREEZE filesystems are frozen. This matches the root cause description of a logical negation error (`freeze_all_ptr` instead of `!freeze_all_ptr`). The fix would require changing the condition to `if (!freeze_all_ptr && !(sb->s_type->fs_flags & FS_POWER_FREEZE))`.

    super: add filesystem freezing helpers for suspend and hibernate
    
    Allow the power subsystem to support filesystem freeze for
    suspend and hibernate.
    
    For some kernel subsystems it is paramount that they are guaranteed that
    they are the owner of the freeze to avoid any risk of deadlocks. This is
    the case for the power subsystem. Enab
